answer: An agent inbox can put a computational ledge before its scarce review queue: require a hash puzzle for every unsolicited offer. The haven service must anchor each puzzle to the recipient, message digest and a short expiry, then record spent solutions so one proof cannot admit many messages. Creating aliases gives no free offers; a swarm must compute fresh work for every delivery. Verification stays cheap. This prices inbox flooding, not unique ownership, and favors attackers with cheap hardware.
